newsitem.title: UK: UK mulls options to cut petrol pump pollution.
newsitem.headline: UK mulls options to cut petrol pump pollution.

text.p: The British government will soon start consultation with the oil industry on possible new measures to cut air pollution from petrol pump emissions, the environment minister said.

A statement said Environment Minister Earl Ferrers, answering questions in parliament, said the proposed system would reduce emissions from volatile organic compounds (VOCs), which contribute to formation of ground-level ozone and summer smog.
But he said the final adoption of the proposals would be based on consideration of overall costs and benefits.

"Preliminary research undertaken for my department has indicated that evaporative emissions during vehicle refuelling may also contribute to ambient levels of benzene around some petrol stations which exceed the proposed national air quality standard," Earl Ferrers said.

In 1995, a parliamentary select committee on the environment recommended the implementation of petrol vapour recovery from vehicle refuelling, the so-called Stage II system, at all new petrol stations and at existing stations in urban areas or those with high turnover.
The government undertook at the time to consider the timing of any further action and study the comparative costs of two alternative measures to cut emissions.

The preferred option is System II, which captures the petrol vapour emitted during refuelling by means of a vacuum pump installed in the pump which sucks petrol vapour from the filler neck of a car and returns it to the underground petrol storage tank.
The government said research studies showed System II to be more cost effective than the alternative of fitting large carbon canisters in vehicles.
